candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

parameters.note: Cliff Lake is not listed in CCR §7.40(b) or §7.50(b), so it falls under the general statewide lake regulation in §5.85(a)(1). It is a high lake in the Meeks Creek chain of northeastern Desolation Wilderness (Lake Tahoe basin), above Lake Genevieve. The general Lake Tahoe tributaries rule §7.50(b)(152) closes Tahoe tributaries seasonally (catch-and-release Sat. before Memorial Day–Sep. 30) only 'upstream to the first lake' — i.e. Meeks Creek below Lake Genevieve — so it does not reach Cliff Lake; the lake itself follows the general lake regulation.

candidates.summary: Open all year (general statewide lake regulation; not listed as a special-regulation water)

candidates.citation: USDA Forest Service — Desolation Wilderness permit program

parameters.description: Cliff Lake lies inside Desolation Wilderness (Meeks Bay Trailhead access). A USDA Forest Service wilderness permit is required year-round for overnight use; a quota applies to overnight destination zones from the Friday before Memorial Day through September 30. Day use is free and unlimited by quota, with a self-issue permit required only when permit boxes are installed at the trailheads (day-use permits are not required in winter, roughly October–March). Bear canisters are required for all overnight visitors.

raw.day_use: free, no quota; self-issue permit when trailhead boxes installed
raw.overnight_quota_season: Friday before Memorial Day through September 30

candidates.summary: Desolation Wilderness permit: required year-round for overnight use (quota Fri. before Memorial Day–Sep. 30); day use free and un-quota'd, self-issue permit when trailhead boxes are installed.

candidates.citation: Sierrafish.com — Cliff Lake (Desolation Wilderness); CDFW 2026 Provisional Stocking Document (Cliff Lake not listed)

parameters.description: Fishery note. A Sierra Nevada lake-fishing database (Sierrafish.com) reports Cliff Lake as 'a Brook Trout water in northeastern Desolation Wilderness'; the same trip report rated fishing 1/10 and described it as 'very lifeless', so brook trout, if present, appear to be at low density. CDFW does not list Cliff Lake in its 2026 Provisional Stocking plan and ended aerial stocking of Desolation Wilderness lakes; any brook trout are a self-sustaining remnant of historical plantings, not a current put-and-take fishery. This is a third-party angler report, not a CDFW fish survey.

candidates.summary: Reported as a brook-trout water by a third-party angler database (fishing rated poor); not currently stocked by CDFW.
